channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: German Power Prices Fall to Lowest Since June on Strong Wind
item.description: German day-ahead power prices fell to their lowest level since June amid strong wind generation, creating an unusual price gap with neighboring France.
item.dc:creator: Eva Brendel

item.title: German Pension Reform May Raise €90 Billion a Year, Apollo Says
item.description: Germany’s historic pension overhaul could increase annual inflows into the system’s three pillars by €90 billion ($105 billion) annually, according to Apollo Global Management Inc. European Economic & Policy Strategist Huw van Steenis.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Kahl

item.title: Fidelity Mandates Five Days in Office as it Opens New Boston Home
item.description: Fidelity is opening a new 735,000-square-foot headquarters in Boston, complete with harbor views, a private bar and an in-office concierge. The move comes as the investment giant ends hybrid work for its Boston employees, requiring them to come into the office five days a week. Greg Ryan reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Air Baltic Puts Polus-Backed Financing Plan to Bondholder Vote
item.description: Air Baltic Corp has asked bondholders to vote next week on proposed stopgap financing backed by Polus Capital Management and Klirmark Capital.
item.dc:creator: Libby Cherry and Edward Clark

item.title: EQT to Pay $2 Billion for Majority Stake in McGill and Partners
item.description: EQT AB has agreed to acquire a majority stake in UK insurance broker McGill and Partners from Warburg Pincus LLC for $2 billion, as the Swedish buyout firm looks to accelerate the company’s global expansion.
item.dc:creator: Charles Daly

item.title: US Stock Futures Steady Ahead of Key August Jobs Data
item.description: US stock futures drifted higher on Friday as traders awaited the crucial August jobs report for more signals about the potential for Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Menton

item.title: Stocks Steady Ahead of Jobs Report; US Retail Diesel Hits Record High | Bloomberg Brief 09/04/2026
item.description: US equity futures and Treasuries hold steady ahead of the August payrolls report. US retail diesel prices rise to a record high as the wars roil the market. DeepSeek plans to deploy at least 160,000 of Huawei’s top accelerators at a massive new data center in Inner Mongolia. Mark Haefele of UBS Global Management and Veronica Clark of Citi join "Bloomberg Brief" to look ahead to the jobs report. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: A Stock-Market Safe Haven Seen as ‘Canary in Coal Mine’ for Risk
item.description: Steadily climbing Treasury yields and a potential Federal Reserve rate hike are threatening to produce more rockiness for utilities, a group that traditionally was one of the stock market’s safest sectors before the AI trade changed the equation.
item.dc:creator: Emily Forgash

item.title: Cocoa Trims Weekly Loss as Deficit Risks Cloud Supply Outlook
item.description: Cocoa futures rose in New York and London, trimming a weekly decline, as the market grapples with the prospect of sufficient short-term supplies being followed by a deficit in the season ahead.
item.dc:creator: Mumbi Gitau and Pratik Parija

item.title: Fire Risks Return to Haunt California’s Utilities
item.description: Investors may have to accept more volatility in the sector as policy reforms are shelved.
item.dc:creator: Brian Eckhouse

item.title: JD Vance Says ‘Proper and Responsible’ for Fed to Lower Interest Rates
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance said on Thursday the Trump administration believes “that the Fed should be lowering interest rates," to help make home ownership more affordable. Michael McKee reports on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: India’s NSE Secures Regulatory Approval for Long-Awaited IPO
item.description: The National Stock Exchange of India Ltd. has received regulatory approval for what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering, clearing a key hurdle in the world’s largest derivatives exchange’s years-long effort to list.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Mascarenhas

item.title: VW Approves Plan for 50K More Layoffs, US Retail Diesel Hits Record | The Opening Trade 9/4/2026
item.description:
Volkswagen’s supervisory board backed a sweeping restructuring that calls for 50,000 additional job cuts, far fewer models and a smaller industrial footprint, giving Chief Executive Officer Oliver Blume his clearest mandate yet to overhaul Europe’s biggest carmaker.
US retail diesel rose to a record, threatening to further spike energy-driven inflation as wars in Iran and Russia roil the market.
The widely used fuel climbed to a nationwide average of $5.85 a gallon at the pump on Thursday, according to the American Automobile Association.
The Opening Trade has everything you need to know as markets open across Europe. With analysis you won't find anywhere else, we break down the biggest stories of the day and speak to top guests who have skin in the game. Hosted by Guy Johnson and Tom Mackenzie. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Soaring Jet Fuel Prices Cool Investor Appetite for Airline Bonds
item.description: As the US-Iran battle escalates, surging jet fuel prices are driving up borrowing costs for airlines, further dimming the prospects for smaller American carriers.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Webster, Stella Mackler and Aaron Weinman

item.title: Volkswagen Plans 50,000 Job Cuts; Anthropic Nears $15B Credit Deal | The Pulse 9/4/2026
item.description:
"The Pulse With Francine Lacqua" is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.
Today's guests: Nouriel Roubini, Roubini Macro Associates CEO; Enrico Letta, Institut Jacques Delors President & Former Italian Prime Minister; Arancha González Laya, Sciences Po Dean of International Affairs & Former Spanish Foreign Minister (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Yield Swings Abate Before Jobs Data After Volatile Week
item.description: US Treasuries posted small moves at the end of a volatile week as bondholders awaited a key jobs report for clues on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.
item.dc:creator: Georgia Hall

item.title: European Stocks Briefly Trim Gains as Hot US Jobs Boost Fed Bets
item.description: European stocks briefly pared gains as traders boosted wagers of a Federal Reserve rate hike following a hotter-than-expected US jobs report. Volkswagen AG shares jumped on plans for a sweeping restructuring at the carmaker.
item.dc:creator: Julien Ponthus

item.title: Anthropic Finalizing $15 Billion Pre-IPO Credit Facility
item.description: Anthropic PBC is set to finalize an expansion of its revolving credit facility to $15 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, clearing a hurdle before the artificial intelligence firm’s public filing for its highly anticipated IPO.
item.dc:creator: Bailey Lipschultz

item.title: Stocks and Bonds Fall as Jobs Fuel Fed-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
item.description: A stronger-than-anticipated increase in US jobs drove stocks and bonds lower as traders boosted their bets the Federal Reserve will raise rates this month.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 4
item.description: Oil was on track for a weekly surge as renewed fighting between the US and Iran heightened concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Paul Burkhardt, Charles Gorrivan and Kanoko Matsuyama
